correctness.rationale: Group base-g digits into H=g³ blocks. For three summands each confined to W0 or W1, every block contribution is s_j+g v_j≤3g(g−1)<H so there is no interblock carry. With q of 3 summands of type W0, q=1 has full interval T1={0,…,2g²−g−1}; q=2,3 are subsets, and q=0 gives multiples-of-g T0 with 3g−2 elements. |T1∩T0|=2g−1, so allowing zeros, size=(2g²−g)^k+(3g−2)^k−(2g−1)^k. A separate digit-allocation proof enforces all three summands positive: only T1 words with quotient digits B=0 and total remainder R≤2 are excluded, exactly binom(k+2,2) weak compositions; T0\T1 all admit 3 positive type-W1 summands. Thus exact formula for every g≥4,k≥1 and θ_g=log_{g³}(2g²−g)<1. Independent direct enumeration verifies nine parameter pairs incl. g=4,k=3 (22599), not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Minimality of a full g-adic basis motivates studying how the representation count deteriorates on removal of an entire infinite digit class. The exact three-exponential inclusion–exclusion law plus polynomial positivity correction and sharp sublinear coverage exponent are natural structural invariants, not a random cutoff table.

final_claim: For g≥4,k≥1, B=A_g(W0)∪A_g(W1) with strictly positive digit-restricted summands and W_r positions ≡r mod3: |3B∩[0,g^{3k})|=(2g²−g)^k+(3g−2)^k−(2g−1)^k−binom(k+2,2), with exponent log_{g³}(2g²−g)<1.
limitations: Only periodic residue classes mod 3 and cutoffs g^{3k}, excludes irregular partitions and arbitrary cutoffs.
